correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed: transform u=cx, compute exact p=uy recurrence and invariant p=1. If p<1, lower-bound p decrements by logarithmic y increments rules out unbounded height, then q(Y)<1 gives exact geometric limit. At p=1, y'=y+1/y and summable renormalized differences yield squared-height log coefficient 1/2. If p>1, y diverges and u decreases; assuming u→0 forces uy→1 by a monotone Riemann-sum tail comparison, contradicting p≥p0>1. Tail sums yield terminal positive velocity, 1/n horizontal correction and +log n/v vertical correction. These arguments cover every positive initial point, with limits/error terms correctly scoped. Standalone exact-rational and numerical checks ran from the present package; finite tests supplement, not replace, the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The parent study emphasizes nonhyperbolic fixed lines and numerical attractor basins. At the distinguished feedback coefficient a=-1, local transverse attraction of every fixed-line point does not determine the global fate: an exact noncompact hyperbola separates fixed-line capture from ballistic escape and carries an intermediate sqrt(n) transient with a log correction. The three-way global phase diagram and sharp time laws are natural dynamical invariants, not an arbitrary finite grid or routine fixed-point computation.
